Eric Boulton (born August 17, 1976) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 15 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Buffalo Sabres, Atlanta Thrashers, New Jersey Devils, and New York Islanders. Before playing in the NHL, Boulton played parts of two seasons with the Oshawa Generals and two seasons with the Sarnia Sting of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 234th overall by the New York Rangers in the 1994 NHL entry draft. He was immediately sent down to play for their ECHL-affiliate Charlotte Checkers and their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Rangers. On October 5, 2000, the Sabres called him up and Boulton made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Chicago Blackhawks. On November 25, Boulton scored his first NHL goal against Mathieu Garon in a 5–3 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On August 20, 2001, Boulton signed a multi-year contract to stay with the Sabres. On August 1, 2003, Boulton signed a two-year contract to stay with the Sabres. On August 8, 2005, Boulton signed a contract to join the Atlanta Thrashers. On June 21, 2006, Boulton signed a contract extension to stay with the Thrashers. On March 20, 2010, Boulton fought Philadelphia Flyers player Ian Laperrière and earned a 5-minute major penalty. This penalty made Boulton the Thrashers' all-time leader in most penalty minutes. On July 7, Boulton signed a one-year, $650,000 contract to stay with the Thrashers. He played parts of six seasons with the Thrashers. On July 15, 2011, Boulton signed a two-year, $1.325 million contract to join the New Jersey Devils. He played a total of 51 games for the Devils. On June 30, 2012, the Devils bought out the rest of Boulton's contract and he became a free agent. On July 2, 2012, Boulton signed a one-year, $540,000 contract to join the New York Islanders. On March 23, 2014, Boulton signed a one-year, $775,000 contract to stay with the Islanders. On October 13, 2015, Boulton signed a one-year, $575,000 contract to stay with the Islanders. On October 13, 2015, Boulton signed a one-year, $575,000 contract to stay with the Islanders. After the 2017 season, Boulton announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Eric Comrie (born July 6, 1995) is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Detroit Red Wings, New Jersey Devils, and Buffalo Sabres. Before playing in the NHL, Comrie played parts of five seasons with the Tri-City Americans of Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 59th overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2013 NHL entry draft. On December 24, 2013, Comrie signed a three-year, $2.77 million entry-level contract to join the Jets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates St. John's IceCaps and Manitoba Moose. On April 5, 2017, the Jets called him up and the next day, Comrie made his NHL debut, stopping 35 of 39 shots in a 5–4 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On April 27, 2022, Comrie stopped all 35 shots he faced to earn his first NHL career shutout in a 4–0 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On September 6, 2018, Comrie signed a one-year, $650,000 contract to stay with the Jets. On September 7, 2019, Comrie signed a two-year, $1.4 million contract to stay with the Jets. On September 30, 2019, the Jets placed Comrie onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Arizona Coyotes. He never played a game for the Coyotes and was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Tucson Roadrunners. On November 30, the Coyotes traded Comrie to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for Vili Saarijärvi. He played 3 regular season games with the Red Wings before being placed back onto waivers. On December 19, 2019, Comrie's contract was picked back up by the Winnipeg Jets. He was sent down to the AHL to play for the Manitoba Moose. After 16 regular season games with the Moose, the Jets placed him back onto waivers. On January 12, 2021, Comrie's contract was picked up by the New Jersey Devils. He only played one regular season game with the Devils before being placed back onto waivers and being picked up again by the Jets on February 18. On July 13, 2022, Comrie signed a two-year, $3.6 million contract to join the Buffalo Sabres. Comrie played parts of two seasons with the Sabres and their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On July 1, 2024, Comrie signed a two-year, $1.65 million contract to rejoin the Winnipeg Jets for a fourth time. Comrie's father Bill Comrie is a businessman who is best known for founding the furniture chain The Brick. He is also half-brothers with both Paul and Mike Comrie whom both were professional hockey player as well.

Eric Nickulas (born March 25, 1975) is an American former professional ice hockey right winger. He played parts of 6 years in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Boston Bruins, St. Louis Blues, and Chicago Blackhawks. He also played in the 3 years in the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL) with the Hannover Scorpions and ERC Ingolstadt. On March 2, 2000, Nickulas would score his first goal in the NHL against Jose Theodore in a 5—2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He won the Calder Cup in 1998 while he was apart of the Boston Bruins farm team, the Providence Bruins.

Eric "Sonja" Nesterenko (October 31, 1933 – June 6, 2022) was a Canadian professional ice hockey centre that played 21 seasons in the National Hockey League. Wilson played 5 seasons with the Toronto Maple Leafs and 16 seasons with the Chicago Black Hawks. He also played for the Chicago Cougars of the World Hockey Association in 1973–74 as well as coached a year in Switzerland. He won the Stanley Cup with the Black Hawks in the 1960-61 NHL season. He retired from professional hockey in 1971 and since that time he has worked as a disc jockey, a stockbroker, a travel broker, a freelance writer, a university professor and a ski instructor. He also acted in the movie, Youngblood, where he played the father of Rob Lowe's character Dean Youngblood. Nesterenko died on June 6, 2022 at the age of 88.

Eric Evan Paterson (September 11, 1929 – January 14, 2014) was a Canadian ice hockey player. He was a member of the Edmonton Mercurys that won a gold medal at the 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo, Norway.

Eric Henry Liddell (; 16 January 1902 – 21 February 1945) was a British Olympic gold medalist runner, Scottish rugby union international player, and Christian missionary. He was born in China to Scottish missionary parents. At the 1924 Summer Olympics in Paris, Liddell refused to run because they were held on a Sunday. Instead he competed in the 400 metres held on a weekday, a race that he won. He returned to China in 1925 to be a missionary teacher. Liddell's Olympic training and racing, and the religious convictions that influenced him, are shown in the Oscar-winning 1981 movie Chariots of Fire, in which he is played by Ian Charleson. Liddell died from brain cancer on 21 February 1945 at the Japanese run Weixian Internment Camp in Weifang at the age of 43.

Eric Weissberg (August 16, 1939 – March 22, 2020) was an American singer, banjo player, and multi-instrumentalist. He was known for his banjo solo in "Dueling Banjos". It was released as a single that reached number 2 in the United States and Canada in 1973. Weissberg was a member of the folk group The Tarriers. Weissberg was born in New York City. Weussberg died on March 22, 2020 in Detroit, Michigan of Alzheimer's disease-related problems, aged 80.

Eric Tinkler (born 30 July 1970) is a South African football coach and former player. Eric Tinkler's style of play is characterized by a front-foot approach and a focus on defensive and finishing. He emphasizes the importance of making better decisions in defense and improving finishing to avert goals. Tinkler believes in playing on the front foot constantly and has been consistent in his approach, even after facing challenges and setbacks. Widely regarded as one of the best South Africa's defensive midfielders. In 1990, he began his career in the South African National Football League. In 1992, the midfielder moved to Viktoria Setúbal, for which he played two seasons in the second division and two seasons in the first division. In 1996 he moved to Cagliari, for whom he played 20 matches in Serie A. In the summer of 1997 he moved to the English Premier League club Barnsley for 650 thousand pounds. He played his first match in the Premier League on August 9, 1997 against West Ham (defeat with a score of 1-2). The South African footballer scored his first goal for the club in a match against Bolton Wanderers on August 27, 1997. Barnsley then won with a score of 2-1. In the 1997/98 season, Eric played 29 (25 in the Premier League, 2 in the Cup, 2 in the League Cup) and scored 2 goals (2 in the Premier League), Barnsley took 19th place and were relegated to the First Division. Eric Tinkler played in the First Division until 2002. From 2002 to 2005 he played for the Portuguese third division club Caldas. In 2005, Eric returned to Wits University and helped the team win the second division and promotion to the Premier League. In 1994, he made his debut in official matches as part of the national team of South Africa. He was the main player of the national team at its home African Cup of Nations in 1996, winning the title of continental champion that year. This victory gave the national team the right to participate in the 1997 Confederations Cup, where Tinkler was also in the application, but did not enter the field. Subsequently, he participated in two more African Cups of Nations - in 2000 in Ghana and Nigeria, as well as in 2002 in Mali. In total, during his career in the national team, which lasted 8 years, he spent 45 matches in its uniform, scoring 1 goal. He began his coaching career, returning to football after a short break, in 2015, heading the coaching staff of the Orlando Pirates club, where he worked from 2015 to 2016. During his coaching career, he also led the teams Cape Town City, Supersport United, Chippa United and Maritzburg United. Since 2021, he has again headed the coaching staff of the Cape Town City team. African Cup of Nations: 1996, 2000; runner-up

Erich Probst (5 December 1927–16 March 1988) was an Austrian footballer. He played as a striker for different teams in Vienna and also abroad. He started with Admira Wien at 17 years old. After a year with Vienna, he signed with SK Rapid Wien. In this time he won the Austrian Championship four times. In his first season with Rapid, he scored 28 goals in 23 matches. Although he was always a top scorer, he never shot the highest number of goals in the league. After his time with Rapid, he went to Wuppertaler SV in Germany. After the relegation of Wuppertal, he went on to Switzerland, playing for FC Zürich. In winter 1959 he came back to Austria to SV Austria Salzburg. The club paid 90,000 Austrian schillings, which was the highest till this time. He shot 15 goals, and the team could stay in the top league. During his time with Salzburg, he played his last match with the national football team. He was the first player of SV Austria Salzburg who ever played for the team. In the 1960/61 season he was coach of SV Austria but not successful. So he went on to play as a striker again. His last clubs were the SAK 1914 in Salzburg and First Vienna FC in Vienna. At all, he scored 150 goals in Austria's top league. He played 19 times for the Austrian national football team and scored 17 goals. His first match was on 27 May 1951 (4:0 versus Scotland). In the qualification match for the FIFA World Cup 1954 versus Portugal, he scored 5 goals for the 9:1 win. He was member of the 1954 FIFA World Cup squad, which reached third place. During the tournament he scored six goals and was together with Max Morlock of Germany and Josef Hügi of Switzerland second in the scorer list. During his time abroad, he was not a player on the team. But in 1960 he played his last match versus France (2:4), where he also scored his last goal for the team. So he was the first national football team player coming from SV Austria Salzburg. Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Probst goal. Joseph Ruud (born November 28, 1981) is an American professional wrestler. He is best known for his time in WWE under the ring name Erick Rowan. He first competed in WWE from 2011 to 2020, where he was a member of The Wyatt Family along with Bray Wyatt, Luke Harper, Daniel Bryan, Braun Strowman and Randy Orton. He began performing as Erick Redbeard on the independent circuit and for All Elite Wrestling, before re-signing with WWE in 2024 and joining The Wyatt Sicks. The Wyatt Sicks. He was released again by WWE in April 2026. Rudd competed in various independent promotions in both the United States and Japan before signing with WWE. In 2007, he worked for Pro Wrestling Noah in Japan under the ring name, Thoruf. After his time with them was done, he returned to the United States and started competing for F1rst Wrestling under the ring name, Thoruf Marius. During his time there he feuded with Brody Hoofer. In 2011, Ruud signed a developmental contract with WWE. He was assigned to their developmental territory Florida Championship Wrestling and started competing under the ring name Erick Rowan. He debuted on FCW TV in August 2011 when he defeated Kenneth Cameron. When FCW changed its name to NXT Wrestling, he debuted on the December 12, 2012 episode of NXT as a follower of Bray Wyatt, who introduced Rowan as his "second son". As a member of the stable The Wyatt Family, Rowan teamed with Wyatt's "first son" Luke Harper. They defeated Percy Watson and Yoshi Tatsu on the January 9, 2013 episode of NXT and defeated them again on the January 23 in the first round of the NXT Tag Team Championship tournament. Rowan and Harper defeated Bo Dallas and Michael McGillicutty in the semi-finals but were defeated in the finals by Adrian Neville and Oliver Grey. Harper and Rowan won a triple threat elimination tag match on May 2 and defeated Neville and Bo Dallas, who filled in for the injured Grey, on the May 8 episode (taped on May 2) to win the tag titles. On June 20, they lost the NXT Tag Team Championship to Adrian Neville and Corey Graves. Starting on May 27, 2013, videos played on Raw to promote the upcoming main roster debut of the Wyatt Family. They debuted on the July 8 episode when they attacked Kane. Rowan made his WWE in-ring debut in a tag team match on the July 26 episode of SmackDown, where he and Harper defeated Tons of Funk (Brodus Clay and Tensai). Rowan and Harper went on a winning streak over many teams for a couple months but suffered their first lost on the October 11 episode of SmackDown from Cody Rhodes and Goldust. On September 29, 2014, Rowan and Harper were "set free" by Wyatt, therefore the Wyatt Family broke up and Rowan began wrestling in singles competition. On the November 17 episode of Raw, Rowan became a face when he joined Team Cena for Survivor Series, while Harper joined Team Authority. At the event, Rowan was eliminated by Harper, with the help of Seth Rollins, but Team Cena later won the match. At the 2015 Royal Rumble, Rowan entered his first Royal Rumble match. Although he lost to Harper in a qualifying match 3 days before on SmackDown, he entered the match anyway after attacking number 6 entrant Curtis Axel before he could make his way to the ring. Rowan was eliminated by Wyatt. After an injury, Rowan returned on the October 19 episode of Raw as a heel when he re-joined the Wyatt Family. On April 3, 2016, at WrestleMania 32, Rowan answered The Rock's challenge to a match, after the Wyatts confronted him. The Rock defeated Rowan in six seconds, which broke the record for the shortest WrestleMania match of all time. On July 19, Rowan was drafted to SmackDown in the 2016 WWE draft along with Wyatt. On April 10, 2017, the Wyatt Family broke up again when Wyatt was moved to Raw in the Superstar Shake-up. On the October 10 episode of SmackDown Live, Rowan and Harper, now wrestling simply under their last names, were reintroduced as the Bludgeon Brothers. They defeated the Hype Bros (Zack Ryder and Mojo Rawley) in their return match on November 21. At WrestleMania 34 on April 8, 2018, they won the SmackDown Tag Team Championship in a Triple threat tag team match also involving champions The Usos (Jey and Jimmy Uso), and The New Day (Big E and Kofi Kingston). This also was Rowan's first main roster championship win. On the August 21 episode of SmackDown Live, they lost the title to The New Day (Kingston and Xavier Woods) in a no disqualification match. After both Rowan and Harper were injured, the Bludgeon Brothers broke up. Rowan returned from injury at the Royal Rumble pay-per-view event on January 27, 2019,helping Daniel Bryan to keep his WWE Championship against AJ Styles. On the May 7 episode of SmackDown Live, Rowan and Bryan defeated The Usos for the vacant SmackDown Tag Team Championship. At Extreme Rules on July 14, they lost the titles to the New Day (Big E and Xavier Woods) in a Triple threat tag team match also involving Heavy Machinery (Otis and Tucker). On September 3, Rowan turned on Bryan. In the 2019 draft on October 14, he was drafted to Raw. On April 15, 2020, he was released from WWE, ending his time in the company after nine years. Following his time WWE, Ruud began wrestling under the ring name "Erick Redbeard". After the death of his friend and former tag team partner Brodie Lee, Redbeard appeared on All Elite Wrestling's (AEW) Brodie Lee Celebration of Life on December 30. He protected members of The Dark Order (a stable previously led by Lee) from being attacked by Wardlow during a six-man tag team match. Redbeard returned to AEW on the March 4, 2022 episode of Rampage and teamed with Death Triangle (Pac and Penta Oscuro). On March 6, they faced the House of Black (Malakai Black, Brody King, and Buddy Matthews) at Revolution's "Buy-In" pre-show event. They lost the match after Redbeard got pinned by Black. On August 25, 2023, Rowan made his return to WWE on SmackDown in a tribute to Bray Wyatt, who died from a heart attack the day before. In May 2024, he signed a contract to return to the company full-time. On the June 17 episode of Raw, Rowan was reintroduced a part of The Wyatt Sicks, the new stable led by Uncle Howdy. His new mask looked like Ramblin' Rabbit from Bray Wyatt's "Firefly Funhouse". On August 5, Rowan won his return match, teaming with his new partners Dexter Lumis and Joe Gacy against American Made (Chad Gable, Julius Creed and Brutus Creed). On April 24, Rowan, along with the other members of the Wyatt Sicks, was again released by WWE. Erica Moyers is an American wheelchair basketball player and sitting volleyball player. She played at the 2004 Summer Paralympics, winning a bronze medal. She is from Athens, Alabama. She played wheelchair basketball for the University of Alabama.

Erich Hof (3 August 1936 – 25 January 1995) was an Austrian footballer and coach. played as a forward mostly for Wiener Sport-Club. He was born in the Brigittenau district of Vienna. Hof began playing football as a striker with SCR Hochstädt. In 1952 he went to Wiener Sport-Club. There he played until 1969. Only 1964/65 he played for FK Austria Wien. In 1959 and 1961 he was top scorer of the Austrian league with 32 and 21 goals. Hof was a leading Austrian footballer in the 1960s and was known as "The Professor of Football" (Der Professor des Fußballs). Hof made 37 appearances and scored 28 goals for the Austria national football team from 1957 to 1968. He made his debut in a friendly match against West Germany on 10 March 1957. Erich Habitzl (9 October 1923 in Vienna – 26 September 2007 in Vienna) was an Austrian footballer. He played mainly for SK Admira Wien. He also played for the Austrian national football team. He took part in the 1948 Olympic Games in London. He started his career with SK Admira Wien in 1939. During the Second World War he had his first championship appearances but the breakthrough did not come until the end of the 1940s. In 1948 he reached the Cup final and scored the only goal for Admira in a 1-2 loss versus Austria Wien. He was the top scorer in the league in 1949. In 1954 he went to France and played for RC Lens. In 1956–57 he played for FC Nantes. He came back to Admira in 1957 and played until 1960. Overall, he scored 146 goals in 194 games for the club. After his career he ran a shoe shop with his brother. In 2009 the district of Floridsdorf honored his services to Austrian football and named an alley after him. The Habitzlgasse was officially opened on 26 September 2009. He made his debut against Sweden on 11 June 1948 where he scored two goals. He was also part of the national team at the 1948 Olympic Games in London. Between 1948 and 1951 he played 11 matches for Austria, scoring 5 goals. In an away match versus Switzerland on 3rd April 1949 he scored the 500th goal of the Austrian national football team. Erich Obermayer (born 23 January 1953, in Wien) is a former Austrian football player. He played for FK Austria Wien and the Austrian national football team as defender. He started his career with FC Wien. At the age of 16 he came to Austria Wien where he stayed for the rest of his career. In his 18 years with Austria he played 544 matches and scored 15 goals. He was chosen in Austria's Team of the Century in 2001. He made his debut for Austria in an April 1975 European Championship qualification match against Hungary and was a participant at the 1978 FIFA World Cup. There he scored a goal in a match against the Netherlands. This was his only goal in the team. He played also in the 1982 FIFA World Cup where he was captain of the team. He played 50 caps and scored one goal. His last international was a March 1985 friendly match against the Soviet Union. Simmeringer SC and FCM Traiskirchen.

Erich Stojaspal (15 March 1929 in Vienna- 30 March 2010) was an Austrian footballer. He played as forward mainly for FK Austria Wien. He started playing football in Simmering with the local club Ostbahn XI. In 1943 he moved to FK Austria Wien. He played with good success as a left winger. However, he was mostly used in the reserve team. In the summer of 1955 he left Austria and moved to Simmeringer SC. He ended his career in 1960. He was the younger brother of Ernst Stojaspal.

Erica Lindbeck (born May 29, 1992) is an American voice actress best known as the third voice of Barbie in the eponymous media franchise, succeeding Kelly Sheridan in 2015 and is also the voice of Loona in Helluva Boss. She was also the boss of Player Voice 2 in Saints Row.

Erik De Vlaeminck (23 March 1945 – 4 December 2015) was a Belgian cyclist. He was a recording-winning cyclo-cross world-champion seven times (in 1966, 1968, 1969, 1970, 1971, 1972, 1973). He was born in Eeklo. He was the brother of Roger De Vlaeminck. Later in life, De Vlaeminck had Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease. He died in Eeklo on 4 December 2015, aged 70.

Erik Donald Stanley Gudbranson (born January 7, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman and alternate captain for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was selected third overall by the Florida Panthers in the 2010 NHL Entry Draft. Gudbranson has previously played for the Florida Panthers, San Antonio Rampage, Vancouver Canucks, Pittsburgh Penguins, Anaheim Ducks, Ottawa Senators, Nashville Predators, and Calgary Flames.

Erik Cole (born November 6, 1978) is an American former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 13 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Carolina Hurricanes, Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens, Dallas Stars, and Detroit Red Wings. Outside of the NHL, Cole played for Eisbären Berlin of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). Cole is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Hurricanes in 2006. He is also a one-time DEL champion, winning with Eisbären Berlin in 2005. Before playing in the NHL, Cole played parts of one season with the Des Moines Buccaneers of the United States Hockey League (USHL), three years with the Clarkson Golden Knights of ECAC Hockey, a two seasons with the Cincinnati Cyclones of the International Hockey League (IHL). He had a successful time with the Golden Knights, being named to the All-ECAC Hockey Rookie Team after finishing his rookie season with 11 goals and recording 20 assists in 34 games. The next season, he was named to the All-ECAC Hockey First Team, AHCA East Second-Team All-American, ECAC Hockey All-Tournament Team and All-ECAC Hockey Second team. He was drafted 71st overall by the Carolina Hurricanes in the 1998 NHL entry draft. On October 5, 2001, Cole made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the New York Rangers. During the game, he also recorded his first NHL career point, assisting on a Sandis Ozoliņš goal. On October 24, Cole scored his first career NHL goal against Manny Fernandez in a 7–3 win against the Minnesota Wild. On March 4, 2006, Cole was injury after a hit by Brooks Orpik and suffered a fractured vertebra in his neck. During his absence, the Hurricanes went on a run in the playoffs, defeating the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils, and Buffalo Sabres. The went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Hurricanes franchise history. Cole was able to return to help in Game 6 of the Finals. On July 1, 2008, the Hurricanes traded Cole to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Joni Pitkänen. He played 63 games with the Oilers, scoring 16 goals and recording 11 assists. On March 4, 2009, the Oilers traded Cole along with a 2009 fifth-round pick back to the Carolina Hurricanes in exchange for Patrick O'Sullivan and a 2009 second-round pick. On July 1, 2009, Cole signed a two-year, $5.8 million contract to stay with the Hurricanes. On July 1, 2011, Cole signed a four-year, $18 million contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. He had a successful 2011–12 season with the Canadiens, scoring 35 goals and recording 61 points for new NHL career-high totals. On February 26, 2013, the Canadiens traded Cole to the Dallas Stars in exchange for Michael Ryder and a 2013 third-round draft pick. On March 1, 2015, the Stars traded Cole to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for Mattias Bäckman, Mattias Janmark-Nylén and a 2015 second-round draft pick. He only played 11 games with the Red Wings, scoring 3 and recording 3 assists. His season was cut short when he was injured with a spinal contusion in a game against the Arizona Coyotes on April 8. On September 20, 2017, Cole signed a one-day contract to return to the Carolina Hurricanes and announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Erik Christensen (born December 17, 1983) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played parts of 7 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Pittsburgh Penguins, Atlanta Thrashers, Anaheim Ducks, New York Rangers, and Minnesota Wild. Outside of the NHL, Christensen played for HC Lev Praha of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) and HV71 of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Christensen is a one-time Le Mat Trophy champion, winning with HV71 in 2017. Before playing in the NHL, Christensen played parts of five seasons with the Kamloops Blazers and one season with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the teams. He was named to the CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game roster in 2002. He finished the 2002–03 season by scoring 54 goals and recording 54 assists for 108 points in 67 games. That season, he was named to the West First All-Star Team, CHL Second All-Star Team, and was awarded the Bobby Clarke Trophy for being the WHL's top scorer. He was drafted 69th overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2002 NHL entry draft. On November 1, 2005, Christensen made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime win over with the New Jersey Devils. Two days later on November 3, Perrin scored his first NHL goal against Rick DiPietro in a 5–1 win against the New York Islanders. On February 26, 2008, the Penguins traded Christensen along with Colby Armstrong, Angelo Esposito, and a 2008 first-round draft pick to the Atlanta Thrashers in exchange for Pascal Dupuis and Marian Hossa. He played parts of two seasons with the Thrashers, scoring 7 goals and recording 16 assists for 23 points. On March 4, 2009, the Thrashers traded Christensen to the Anaheim Ducks in exchange for Eric O'Dell. He played parts of two seasons with the Ducks, scoring 2 goals and recording 7 assists for 9 points. On July 1, 2009, Christensen signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to stay with the Ducks. On December 2, Christensen was picked up off waivers by the New York Rangers. On July 1, 2010, Christensen signed a two-year, $1.85 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On February 3, 2012, the Rangers traded Christensen along with a conditional 2013 seventh-round draft pick to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for Casey Wellman. He scored 6 goals and recorded 1 assist in 29 games for the Wild. On June 5, 2012, Christensen decided to leave North America and signed a two-year contract with HC Lev Praha of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He played parts of two seasons with the team. On October 22, 2013, Christensen moved to HV71 of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He played parts of four seasons with HV71 and won the Le Mat Trophy with them in 2017. Christensen retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2017.

Erik Haula (born 23 March 1991) is a Finnish professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Carolina Hurricanes, Florida Panthers, Boston Bruins, and New Jersey Devils. Internationally, Haula plays for Finland. He won a bronze medal with them in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Haula played one season with Omaha Lancers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Gophers, he was named to the All-WCHA Second Team. He was drafted 182nd overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2009 NHL entry draft. On 7 April 2013, Haula signed a two-year, $1.8 million entry-level contract to join the Wild. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Houston Aeros. On 29 November 2013, the Wild called him up and Haula made his NHL debut in a 3–1 loss against the Colorado Avalanche. During the game, he recorded his first NHL point by assisting on a Dany Heatley goal. On 8 October 2013, Haula scored his first NHL goal against Kari Lehtonen in a 3–2 overtime win against the Dallas Stars. On 2 August 2015, Haula signed a two-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Wild. On 21 June 2017, the Wild left Haula unprotected in the 2017 NHL expansion draft and he was selected by the Vegas Golden Knights. The same day, Haula signed a three-year, $8.25 million contract to stay with the Knights. He helped the Knights when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Los Angeles Kings, San Jose Sharks, and Winnipeg Jets on route to their first Stanley Cup Final appearance in Golden Knights franchise history. They were eventually defeated by the Washington Capitals four games to one in the Finals. On 26 June 2019, the Knights traded Haula to the Carolina Hurricanes in exchange for Nicolas Roy and a 2021 conditional fifth-round draft pick. He scored 12 goals and recorded 10 assists for 22 points in 41 regular season games for the Hurricanes. On 26 June 2019, the Hurricanes traded Haula along with Lucas Wallmark, Eetu Luostarinen and Chase Priskie to the Florida Panthers in exchange for Vincent Trocheck. He played 7 regular season games and recorded 2 assists, as well as, 4 playoff games where he scored 1 goal. On 23 December 2020, Haula signed a one-year, $1.75 million contract to join the Nashville Predators. He played one season with the Predators. On 28 July 2021, Haula signed a two-year, $4.75 million contract to join the Boston Bruins. He played one season with the Bruins. On 8 July 2022, the Bruins traded Haula along with to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Pavel Zacha. He played parts of three seasons with the Devils. On 18 June 2025, the Devils traded Haula back to the Nashville Predators in exchange for Jeremy Hanzel and a 2025 fourth-round draft pick.

Erik Gustafsson (born 14 March 1992) is a Swedish professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks, Calgary Flames, Philadelphia Flyers, Montreal Canadiens, Washington Capitals, Toronto Maple Leafs, New York Rangers, and Detroit Red Wings. Outside of the NHL, Gustafsson played for Lokomotiv Yaroslavl and Frölunda HC of the Elitserien/Swedish Hockey League (SEL). Before playing in the NHL, Gustafsson played one season with Lokomotiv Yaroslavl and two seasons with Frölunda HC of the Elitserien/Swedish Hockey League (SEL). He was drafted 93rd overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 2012 NHL entry draft. He never played a game for the Oilers. On 30 April 2015, Gustafsson signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rockford IceHogs. On 30 October 2015, the Blackhawks called him up and Gustafsson made his NHL debut in a 5–4 loss against the Minnesota Wild. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Artem Anisimov goal. On 20 January 2018, Gustafsson scored his first NHL goal against Jaroslav Halák in a 7–3 loss against the New York Islanders. On 14 July 2017, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $650,000 entry-level contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On 6 March 2018, Gustafsson signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On 24 February 2020, the Blackhawks traded Gustafsson to the Calgary Flames in exchange for a 2020 third-round draft pick. He recorded 3 assists in 7 regular season games and 4 assists in ten playoff games. On 12 October 2020, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $3 million contract to join the Philadelphia Flyers. He scored 1 goal and recorded 9 assists in 24 regular season games with the Flyers. On 10 October 2021, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $800,000 contract to rejoin the Chicago Blackhawks. He scored 3 goals and recorded 15 assists in 59 regular season games in his return with the Blackhawks. On 13 July 2022, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $800,000 contract to join the Washington Capitals. On 17 December, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–2 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On 28 February 2023, the Capitals traded Gustafsson along with a 2023 first-round draft pick to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Rasmus Sandin. He recorded 4 assists in 9 regular season games and 1 goal in 2 playoffs games with the Leafs. On 1 July 2023, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $825,000 contract to join the New York Rangers. He scored 6 goals and recorded 25 assists in 76 regular season games and recorded 3 assists in 16 playoff games with the Rangers. On 1 July 2024, Gustafsson signed a two-year, $4 million contract to join the Detroit Red Wings. He scored 2 goals and recorded 16 assists over parts of two seasons with the Red Wings. On 1 July 2026, Gustafsson signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Los Angeles Kings.

Erik Sven Gunnar Karlsson (born 31 May 1990) is a Swedish professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Pittsburgh Penguins of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators and San Jose Sharks. Outside of the NHL, Karlsson played for Frölunda HC of the Elitserien and Jokerit of the SM-liiga. Karlsson is a three-time James Norris Memorial Trophy, winning in 2012, 2015, and 2023. He is also a seven-time All-Star game, being named one in 2011, 2012, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2023. Internationally, Karlsson plays for Sweden, winning a silver medal in 2014. Before playing in the NHL, Karlsson played parts of two seasons with Frölunda HC of the Elitserien. He was drafted 15th overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2008 NHL entry draft. On 7 May 2009, Karlsson signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Senators. On 3 October 2009, Ottawa called him up and Karlsson made his NHL debut in a 5–2 loss against the New York Rangers. During the game, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Peter Regin goal. On 19 December, Karlsson scored his first NHL goal against Niklas Bäckström in a 4–1 win against the Minnesota Wild. He finished the 2011–12 season scoring 19 goals and recording 59 assists for 78 points in 81 regular seasons games. He also scored a goal in 7 playoff games. He was named to the All-Star game and was awarded the James Norris Memorial Trophy for top defensive player in the NHL. That season, he also set Senators franchise records for most assists by a defenceman in a single season and most points by a defenceman in a single season. On 19 June 2012, Karlsson signed a seven-year, $45.5 million contract to stay with the Senators. During a game against the Pittsburgh Penguins, Matt Cooke hit Karlsson into the boards and stomped on the back of his ankle with his skate blade. The caused Karlsson's Achilles tendon to sever and he required surgery which caused him to miss the rest of the season. On 2 October 2014, the team named Karlsson as the 9th captain in Senators franchise history. He won his second James Norris Memorial Trophy that season. On 6 January 2016, he was named to his third All-Star game. The next season, Karlsson set Senators franchise records for most career goals by a defenceman, most career points by a defenceman, most career assists by a defenceman, most consecutive games played, and most career overtime winners scored by a defenceman. On 12 June 2018, controversy surrounded both Karlsson and the team. Karlsson's wife Melinda Currey decided to file a protection order against Monika Caryk, the girlfriend of teammate Mike Hoffman. Karlsson's wife accused Caryk of cyberbullying and harassment before and after the death of Karlsson's son. She accused her of creating fake accounts online and sending over 1,000 comments towards the Karlssons, which also included some being made about the stillbirth of the Karlssons' son. Both Karlsson and Hoffman were traded because of the controversy. On September 13, 2018, the Senators traded Karlsson along with Francis Perron to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Rūdolfs Balcers, Dylan DeMelo, Josh Norris, Chris Tierney, a 2019 second-round draft pick, and a 2020 first-round draft pick. On 2 January 2019, he was named to his sixth All-Star game. On 17 June, Karlsson signed a eight-year, $92 million contract to stay with the Sharks, which at the time made him both the third highest-paid player in the league at time of signing and the then-highest-paid defenceman in league history. He had a successful 2022–23 season. He was named to his seventh All-Star game and was awarded his third James Norris Memorial Trophy. On 1 November 2022, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–5 shootout loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On 6 August 2023, the Sharks traded Karlsson along with Dillon Hamaliuk and a 2026 third-round draft pick to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Mikael Granlund, Mike Hoffman, Jan Rutta, and either a 2024 conditional or 2025 first-round draft pick.
Erik Nevland (born 10 November 1977) is a Norwegian former professional footballer who played as a forward. He is currently the sporting director of Viking.

Erik Meijs (April 20, 1991 in Zoetermeer - November 16, 2017 in Duisburg, Germany) was a Dutch male badminton player. Meijs became Dutch junior master in badminton men's single in 2010, and Dutch master in badminton men's single in 2016. He died of the wounds caused by a car accident in 2017, at the age of 26.

Erika "Riki" Mahringer (16 November 1924 – 30 October 2018) was an Austrian former alpine skier. She was born in Linz, Austria. She competed in the 1948 and 1952 Winter Olympics. In 1948 she won the bronze medal in the slalom event as well as in the Alpine combined competition. In the downhill contest she finished 19th. Four years later she finished fourth in the 1952 Olympic downhill event. Mahringer died on 30 October 2018 in Innsbruck, Austria from heart failure at the age of 93.

Erika Lava is an Italian water polo player and coach. She was a member of the Italian women's national water polo team. She played at the 2003 European Waterpolo Championship, 2003 FINA World Championships, and 2004 FINA Women’s Water Polo Superfinal.

Eriko Arakawa is a Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Arakawa was born in Nerima, Tokyo on October 30, 1979. In 1997, she joined Nadeshiko League club Yomiuri-Seiyu Beleza (later Nippon TV Beleza) from youth team. She was selected Best Eleven in 2003 and 2004. In the September 2008 WPS International Draft, she was drafted by FC Gold Pride in the top level US based Women's Professional Soccer league. In her first appearance for FC Gold Pride, Arakawa scored the club's first ever goal against Boston Breakers leading to a 2–1 victory. It would turn out to be her only goal of the season. Following the end of the 2009 WPS season, she was back to Nippon TV Beleza. In 2010, she moved to Urawa Reds Ladies. From 2013, she played for Chifure AS Elfen Saitama (2013-2014, 2016), Nippon TV Beleza (2015) and Nippon Sport Science University Fields Yokohama (2017). She is currently playing for Chifure AS Elfen Saitama from 2018. On 10 June 2000, Arakawa debuted for the Japan national team against Canada. She was a member of Japan for 2003, 2007 World Cup, 2004 and 2008 Summer Olympics. She played 72 games and scored 20 goals for Japan until 2011.

Eriko Sato is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Sato was born in Shizuoka Prefecture on November 25, 1985. After graduating from Waseda University, she played for TEPCO Mareeze. On July 27, 2003, when Sato was 17 years old, she debuted for the Japan national team against Australia. She played 2 games for Japan until 2008.

Erika Fisch (29 April 1934 – 9 November 2021) was a German athlete. She represented the United Team of Germany at the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne. She came in fourth place in the long jump. During the 1962 European Athletics Championships she won silver in the 4 × 100 m relay. Fisch died on 9 November 2021, at the age of 87.
Erika Fairweather is a swimmer from New Zealand. Fairweather competed at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships and the 2020 Summer Olympics. She was born on 31 December 2003.

Erik ten Hag (born 2 February 1970) is a Dutch professional football manager. and former player. He is currently the technical director of Eredivisie club Twente. Ten Hag played as a centre-back. He started his career withHe joined De Graafschap in 1990. He won the Eerste Divisie in his first season there. He went back to Twente in 1992. He moved to RKC Waalwijk two years later and stayed for one season. He started playing at Utrecht in 1995. Ten Hag went back to Twente for a third time in 1996. He won the KNVB Cup in 2001. He retired in 2002, at age 32. Ten Hag started his career as a manager in 2012 at Go Ahead Eagles. He helped the club to promotion to the Eredivisie in his first season. He then joined Bayern Munich II in 2013. He won promotion to the Regionalliga Bayern in 2014. He went back to the Netherlands in 2015to be sporting director and head coach at Utrecht. He joined Ajax in 2017. He won three Eredivisie titles and two KNVB Cups. He also led the team to the semi-finals of the 2018–19 UEFA Champions League. In 2022, he became the manager of Manchester United. In his first season with the club, United won the EFL Cup. He also reached the final of the FA Cup, but his team lost against Manchester City. On 28 October 2024, he was sacked by Manchester United. He would later be hired by Bayer 04 Leverkusen on 1 July 2025, but would be sacked two months later, after only three games in charge. Erik Černák (born 28 May 1997) is a Slovak professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Tampa Bay Lightning of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Černák played for HC Košice of the Slovak Extraliga. Černák is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning in 2020 and 2021. Before playing in the NHL, Černák played two seasons with the HC Košice of the Slovak Extraliga and two seasons with the Erie Otters of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. With Košice, he won back-to-back championships in 2014 and 2015. He was drafted 43rd overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On 14 July 2015, Černák signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He never played a game with the Kings. On 26 February 2017, the Kings traded Černák along with Peter Budaj, a 2017 seventh-round raft pick, and a 2017 conditional pick to the Tampa Bay Lightning in exchange for Ben Bishop and a 2017 fifth-round draft pick. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On 13 November 2018, the Lightning called him up and Černák made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Buffalo Sabres. On 19 November, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Victor Hedman goal in a 3–2 loss against the Nashville Predators. On 2 February 2019, Černák scored his first NHL goal against Henrik Lundqvist in a 3–2 win against the New York Rangers. On 26 November 2019, the league suspended Černák for 2 regular season games and fined him $7,500 for elbowing Buffalo Sabres player Rasmus Dahlin during a game. Erina Yamane is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Yamane was born in Hiroshima on December 20, 1990. After graduating from JFA Academy Fukushima, she joined TEPCO Mareeze based in Fukushima Prefecture club in 2009. However, the club was disbanded for Fukushima nuclear disaster in 2011. She moved to JEF United Chiba in 2012.She played 92 matches in Nadeshiko League. She left the club in July 2017. In August, she joined Spanish Primera División club Real Betis. She played for the club in 2 seasons. In August 2019, she returned to JEF United Chiba. She retired end of 2020 season. In November 2008, Yamane was selected the Japan U-20 national team for 2008 U-20 World Cup. On January 15, 2010, she debuted for the Japan national team against Chile. In July, she was selected Japan U-20 team for 2010 U-20 World Cup. In 2014, she was a member for 2014 Asian Cup and 2014 Asian Games. Japan won the championship at Asian Cup and the 2nd place at Asian Games. In 2015, she also played at 2015 World Cup and Japan won the 2nd place. She played 26 games for Japan until 2019.
Erin Attwell (born 12 March 1999) is a Canadian track cyclist. She competed at the 2018 UCI Track Cycling World Championships, 2019 Pan American Games, and 2021 UCI Track Cycling World Championships.

Eris Aragoza, (born on February 27, 1996) is a Filipino actor, host, dancer and singer in the Philippines, He is currently a host in the variety Philippine noontime show in It's Showtime Online U at Kapamilya ABS-CBN Network. Aragoza was born and raised in Binangonan, province of Rizal, at the age of 23 he joined at the segment of BidaMan in August 23, 2019 at It's Showtime at the placed of 2nd runner up. 2021 - Your Momshies, Your Soul is Mine as Banchong

Erland Kops (14 January 2017 – 17 February 2017) was a Danish badminton player. He was one of the best players of the sport. He was best known for winning eleven titles at the All England Open Badminton Championships, between 1958 and 1969. He also played 44 national matches for Denmark from 1957 to 1972. He was added to the Badminton Hall of Fame in 1997. He was born in Copenhagen. Kops died on 17 February 2017, at the age of 80.

Erling Braut Haaland (né Håland; born 21 July 2000) is a Norwegian professional footballer. He plays as a striker for Premier League club Manchester City and the Norway national team. Haaland was born in Leeds, England. His father, Alf-Inge "Alfie" Håland, is a former player who played as a defender and midfielder. The family returned to Alfie's hometown of Bryne, Norway when Erling was 3 years old. Erling Haaland started his career at his hometown club Bryne in 2016. He moved to Molde in 2017 where he spent two years. In January 2019, Austrian club Red Bull Salzburg signed him on a five-year contract. In the 2019–20 UEFA Champions League, he became the first teenager to score in five straight Champions League matches and the second teenager to score 10 goals in the competition. He won the Austrian Bundesliga twice and the Austrian Cup once with Salzburg. In December 2019, Haaland joined Borussia Dortmund for a fee reported in the region of €20 million. Erling Haaland is known for his speed, strength, positioning, and goalscoring ability. He is considered one of the best strikers in the world. After joining Manchester City in 2022, Haaland broke several goalscoring records in English football. In his first Premier League season, he scored 36 league goals, which was a new competition record. Haaland has also broken records in the UEFA Champions League. He became the fastest player to reach 50 goals in the competition. He is also Norway's all-time top goalscorer for the national team. Ernest Cotton Deane (born 4 May 1887 and died 25 September 1915) was a medical officer of the British Indian Army. He was born in the city of Limerick, Ireland. He went to school in Dún Laoghaire (then called Kingstown) in County Dublin. Deane studied medicine at the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland, graduating in 1909. He played rugby for Ireland in one match, against England in February 1909. However, his rugby career was cut short after he broke his leg soon after in a game against Oxford University. Deane became a surgeon at the Adelaide Hospital, Dublin. He was then commissioned into the Royal Army Medical Corps in 1911. In 1913, he was posted to India and served in Burma. He was sent to Meerut at the start of the First World War. He went to France with the Garhwal Brigade of the Indian Expeditionary Force. They arrived in Marseilles in September 1914. He was then sent immediately to the Western Front. There he served first with the 20th Field Ambulance. Then he served as a medical officer of the 2nd Battalion, The Royal Leicestershire Regiment. His unit saw much active service. On 22 August 1915, he was awarded the Military Cross after running out under machine gun fire to rescue four men who had been wounded by artillery fire. A month later, his regiment participated in the Battle of Loos, and was almost entirely destroyed. He was shot dead after going to help some injured soldiers. His action earned him a mention in dispatches.

Ernest "Ernie" Banks (January 31, 1931 – January 23, 2015) was a former Major League Baseball player. He was a shortstop and a first baseman. He spent his entire 19-year career with the Chicago Cubs of the National League (1953–1971). He hit 512 home runs in his career. Very few players have hit more than 500 home runs in their careers. He was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1977. He was known as "Mr. Cub". In 2013, he was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Barack Obama. Banks was born in Dallas, Texas and went to Booker T. Washington High School in that city. He was a very good athlete. He won "letters" in football, basketball and track. He graduated in 1950. Banks signed with the Kansas City Monarchs of the Negro American League in 1950. He broke into the Major Leagues in 1953 with the Chicago Cubs. He was their first black player. He played for the Cubs his entire career. He started at shortstop, then moved to first base in 1962. In 1955, he set the record for grand slam home runs in a single season with five. That record stood for over thirty years. Banks won the National League Most Valuable Player Award twice, in 1958 and 1959. He became the first shortstop in the history of the National League to win the MVP award in back to back seasons. On May 12, 1970, at Chicago's Wrigley Field, Banks hit his 500th career home run. Banks finished his career with 512 home runs, and his 277 homers as a shortstop were the most ever at the time of his retirement. (Cal Ripken, Jr. now holds the record for most homers as a shortstop with 345.) Banks holds Cubs records for games played (2,528), at-bats (9,421), extra-base hits (1,009), and total bases (4,706). During Banks' career, the Cubs as a team often played poorly. They started to play better late in his career, but they never got into the playoffs. Banks holds the Major League record for most games played without a playoff appearance (2,528). In 1977 Banks was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame. The beginning of Banks' speech that August 8 can be heard on a CD called Baseball's Greatest Hits Vol. II. Commissioner of Baseball Bowie Kuhn presents Banks, who then says, "Thank you very much, Commissioner, for the fine introduction. We've got the setting - sunshine, fresh air; we've got the team behind us so... Let's play two!" Banks had worn number 14 on his Cubs uniform. In 1982 he became the first Cubs players whose number was retired by the team. On March 31, 2008, a statue of Banks was put outside Wrigley Field. The base of the statue repeats his famous saying, "Lets play two!" Banks died of a heart attack at a Chicago hospital on January 23, 2015, eight days before his 84th birthday. His death was announced by his lawyer in that same day. He was buried in Graceland Cemetery, just a few blocks north of Wrigley Field.

Ernest Leslie Dickens (June 25, 1921 – September 27, 1985) was a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman that played 6 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played 2 seasons with the Toronto Maple Leafs and 4 seasons with the Chicago Black Hawks. Dickens won the Stanley Cup with the Toronto Maple Leafs in 1942. He was also named to the AHL First All-Star Team in 1947 and was named a “Honoured Member” of the Manitoba Hockey Hall of Fame.

Ernest Gilbert Broglio (; August 27, 1935 – July 16, 2019) was an American professional baseball pitcher. He played for the St. Louis Cardinals and Chicago Cubs of Major League Baseball from 1959 to 1966. He was born in Berkeley, California. Broglio was best known as the "other player" in the controversial trade that sent future Baseball Hall of Fame outfielder Lou Brock from the Cubs to the Cardinals in June 1964. Broglio died on July 16, 2019 from cancer in San Jose, California at the age of 83.

Ernest Ferrell Bowman (July 28, 1935 – August 4, 2019) was an American professional baseball player. He was an infielder who appeared in 165 games in Major League Baseball for the San Francisco Giants from 1961 to 1963. He retired in 1969. Bowman died at his home in Johnson City, Tennessee on August 4, 2019 at the age of 84.

Ernesto Marcel (23 May 1948 – 29 June 2020) was a Panamanian professional boxer. He competed from 1966 to 1974. He held the WBA featherweight title from 1972 to 1974 and challenged for the WBC featherweight title in 1971. Marcel was born in Colón, Panama. Marcel died on 29 June 2020 in Panama City, aged 72.

Ernesto Antonio Contreras Vásquez (19 June 1937 – 25 October 2020) was an Argentine cyclist. He competed at the 1960, 1964 and the 1968 Summer Olympics. He also won the Argentine National Road Race Championships in 1959, 1970 and 1971. He was born in Mendoza, Argentina. Contreras died on 25 October 2020 from a heart attack caused by COVID-19 in Mendoza, aged 83.
Ernesto Gutiérrez was a footballer from Argentina. Ernesto played for the Argentina national football team. He was born on 9 November 1927 and died on 9 December 2006.

Ernesto Alberto Mascheroni Castiglioni (; 21 November 1907 – 3 July 1984) was a footballer from Uruguay. Born in Montevideo, Ernesto was a defender. He played as a left-back. Mascheroni was a complete left-back with his ability to man-mark opponents with success, he was known for his leadership and fine technique. Widely considered as one of the best left-backs of all time. At the time, Mascheroni played for Olimpia, being the only one that this club ceded to the Uruguayan national team for any FIFA World Cup. The team had been fifth in the Uruguayan championship of 1929 and was extinguished in 1933, when it merged with the Capurro club to form the current Uruguayan River Plate. After the World Cup, Mascheroni went to play for Peñarol. There was no Uruguayan championship in 1930 due to the World Cup. In 1931, Mascheroni was not yet a starter, with the black and white defense duo being composed of Adhemar Canavesi and Alberto Noguéz. The team did not have a good championship and even failed to perform in the final two rounds, in a tournament won by Montevideo Wanderers. The starting XI came in 1932, in a duo with Noguéz. This time, the title came, in what was the first professional championship in Uruguayan football. In 1933, the team came close to a new title, only defined after several shootouts with archrival Nacional, held the following year. The black and white even complained that this was only possible due to the cancellation of a legitimate goal in the last regular round, against Sud América. Mascheroni was an absolute starter, with the other flank of the defense being alternated between Noguéz and Lorenzo Fernández. Mascheroni also defended Peñarol in a few games in 1934, the year in which he went to play briefly in Argentine football for Independiente. His place at Peñarol, again runners-up to arch-rivals in 1934, was taken by Héctor Cazenave, later a player for the French national team at the 1938 FIFA World Cup. From Independiente, Mascheroni went to Italy to play for Internazionale, at the time called Ambrosiana. The Milan team had acquired at the time another Uruguayan from Independiente, Roberto Porta, and already had another Uruguayan player, Faccio. The three even defended the Italian national team. Despite twice defending the Azzurri, Mascheroni did not stand out much among the most successful Uruguayans in calcio. Many foreign players of Italian origin had left the country with the outbreak of the Second Italo-Ethiopian War in 1935, fearful of being drafted into the Italian Armed Forces. Mascheroni returned to Uruguay in 1937, returning to Peñarol. That same year, he was Uruguayan champion, although the starting defensive duo was Jorge Clulow and Mario Barradas. The achievement was repeated the following year, this time with Mascheroni starting alongside Clulow, in what was a fourth consecutive championship for Peñarol, who in the same year stood out for a 7–2 victory over Estudiantes de La Plata in the Rio-Pratense Night Tournament. The defender stopped playing in 1940, still as a black and white player, although he had lost the position; Barradas, Clulow and Agustín Prado were the defenders who took turns in the starting lineup the most in 1939 and 1940. Mascheroni was in the 1929 Copa América, but did not play, in the reserve of Pedro Arispe and José Nasazzi, the starting defensive duo in the second Olympic championship in 1924 and 1928. His debut for the Uruguayan national team only took place on July 21, 1930, in the middle of the 1930 FIFA World Cup, in the second match. From then on, he started the rest of the tournament, in a duo with Nasazzi. Although his last game for Uruguay took place on February 12, 1939, he played only thirteen times for the country. He was throughout the 1930s for foreign teams (Independiente and Internazionale) and only in the 1970s would the national team start to admit calling up those who played abroad - the coach of the change, curiously, was Roberto Porta. While playing for Inter, Mascheroni twice played for the Italian national team, also defended by Porta himself. The two matches for the Azzurri took place in 1935. They beat France 2-1 in a friendly in Rome, in a lineup that also included Argentines Enrique Guaita and Alejandro Scopelli, on February 17; and won 2–0 against Austria for the Dr. Gerö Cup, again alongside other South Americans: Uruguayan Ricardo Faccio and Argentinians Enrique Guaita, Atilio Demaría and Raimundo Orsi. Uruguay would refuse to take part in the 1938 FIFA World Cup, officially still in retaliation for the large absence of the European powers in the 1930 edition. The date of February 12, 1939, when Mascheroni last defended the national team, was valid for the last commitment of the Celeste in the Copa America that year. The title went to the host Peru, due to the direct clash in the last round. In times of less profitable professionalism of the activity of a soccer player, Mascheroni, specialized in elevator mechanics, freely chose not to become a coach but an elevator operator. To the Brazilian press, fifty years after the 1930 FIFA World Cup title, he pointed out that, similarly, José Nasazzi "cut marble, helping to constitute the Legislative Palace" and that José Pedro Cea "made a living loading and unloading ice. They were giants, believe me". About not having followed a path as a technician, he justified: "for what, if I already drove elevators? Then, technician, just technical to have the portrait in the newspapers, what good is it? I want to see the coach training players, discovering talents. Do you know why talents are so lacking these days? Because technicians are incapable of revealing them, of discovering them. Do you know anyone who does this as it was done in the past? I bet not." At the time of 1980, when he made the above statements, he was famous as the last Uruguayan still alive of the 1930 champion team. Two other survivors that the first World Cup still had, the Peruvian Antonio Maquilón and the Brazilian Oswaldo Barros Velloso, joined him in a tribute held on the occasion of the decision of the 1980 Mundialito de futebol. It was Mascheroni who kicked off the final. By the time of his death in July 1984, at the age of 76, he was the last surviving member of Uruguay's 1930 World Cup winning team; though it would be another 26 years before the death of the last surviving participant of that World Cup. South American Championship: Runner-up 1939 Central European International Cup: 1933-35

Ernest Joseph Beck (December 11, 1931 – December 12, 2024) was an American professional basketball player. He was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Beck played seven years in the National Basketball Association for the Philadelphia Warriors, St. Louis Hawks, and Syracuse Nationals from 1953 to 1961. Beck died in West Chester, Pennsylvania on December 12, 2024, one day after his 93rd birthday.

Ernesto Grillo (1 October 1929 – 18 June 1998) was an Argentine footballer. He played as a midfielder for Independiente and Boca Juniors in Argentina, and AC Milan in Italy. He was also capped 20 times for Argentina and played in two South American Championships, including the 1955 edition, which Argentina won. Grillo died on 18 June 1998, at the age of 68.

Ernesto Bernardo "Tito" Cucchiaroni (16 November 1927 – 4 July 1971) was an Argentine footballer. He played as a left winger for Rivadavia de Lincoln, Tigre and Boca Juniors in in Argentina, and for Sampdoria and AC Milan in Italy. He was also capped 11 times for Argentina and played in two South American Championships, including the 1955 edition, which Argentina won.

Ernesto de Figueiredo Cordeiro (6 July 1937 – 13 December 2025) was a Portuguese footballer. He played as a striker, and was an amateur player until he was 23, when he joined Sporting CP in 1960. With Sporting CP, he scored 147 goals in 232 matches, and helped them win the 1963–64 European Cup Winners' Cup against MTK Budapest. He would join Vitória de Setúbal in 1968, and played there until he retired in 1970. Figueiredo was capped six for Portugal, and made his debut on 21 June 1966, in a friendly match against Denmark. He was part of Portugal's team at the 1966 FIFA World Cup, although he did not play at the tournament. After retiring from football, he worked as a taxi driver. Figueiredo died on 13 December 2025, at the age of 88.

Ernst Franz Hermann Happel (29 November 1925 – 14 November 1992) was a former Austrian football player and football coach. He played for SK Rapid Wien, RC Paris and the Austria national team. Happel started professionally at the age of 17 with SK Rapid Wien as defender. He played only from 1955 till 1956 for another club. In 1999 he was elected for Rapids team of the century. He played his first match for Austria in September 1947 against Hungary. He was a member of the squad for the 1954 World Cup in Switzerland and the 1958 World Cup in Sweden. His last match was in September 1958 against Yugoslavia. He played 51 times in the team and shot 5 goals. Belgian Championship: 1975–76, 1976–77, 1977–78 Scores and results list Austria's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Happel goal.

Ernest Johnson, Jr. (born November 5, 1956) is a sportscaster for ESPN coverage on ABC, TBS, truTV and CBS Sports. He calls play-by-play for Golf on TNT and MLB on TBS. He is also the studio host for the NBA on TNT and college basketball tournaments for Turner Sports and CBS Sports. Johnson called Atlanta Braves games from 1993-1996 and again in 2010. He was also the studio host for TNT's coverage of the Wimbledon Championships. He also worked on Olympic Games and Goodwill Games for Turner Sports. He was a co-host for Charles Barkley's talk show "Listen Up". Johnson also called weightlifting at the 2000 Summer Olympics for NBC. Johnson has called occasional NBA games for TNT. Johnson is the son of the late pitcher for the Milwaukee Braves Ernie Johnson Sr.

Ernest Maurice "Ernie" Vandeweghe Jr. (September 12, 1928 – November 8, 2014) was an American physician, a United States Air Force veteran and professional basketball player. He was best known for playing for the New York Knicks of the NBA. He and his wife Colleen Kay Hutchins (Miss America for 1952) are the parents of former NBA All-Star (and former New Jersey Nets coach) Kiki Vandeweghe and grandfather of tennis professional Coco Vandeweghe. Vandeweghe died at the age of 86 on November 8, 2014 in Newport Beach, California.

Roger Patrick "Ernie" Hunt (17 March 1943 – 20 June 2018) was an English footballer. He played in the Football League for Swindon Town, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Everton, Coventry City, Doncaster Rovers and Bristol City, and for the Los Angeles Wolves in the United Soccer Association. At international level, he was capped three times for the England under-23 team. Hunt died in Gloucestershire on 20 June 2018 of complications from Alzheimer's disease, aged 75.

Ernie Gonzalez (February 19, 1961 – May 15, 2020) was an American professional golfer. He played on the PGA Tour in the 1980s. He won the only title of his career in 1986. He became only the third left-handed golfer to win a Tour event. He was born in San Diego, California. Gonzalez died on May 15, 2020 in Chicago of Alzheimer's disease-related problems, aged 59.

Ernest Rixon Phythian (16 July 1942 – 3 August 2020) was an English professional footballer. He played as a striker. His career lasted between 1960 and 1968. Phythian made over 250 appearances in the Football League, scoring nearly 100 goals. He later played for Wrexham and Hartlepools United before moving to South Africa to play with Southern Suburbs. Phythian died on 3 August 2020, aged 78, in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Ernie Lively (born Ernest Wilson Brown Jr.; January 29, 1947 – June 3, 2021) was an American actor and acting coach. He was known as the father of actors Eric Lively and Blake Lively. Lively was born in Baltimore, Maryland. Lively may be best known for his roles in Passenger 57, The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants and The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants 2. Lively died on June 3, 2021 from heart failure in Los Angeles, aged 74.

Ernst Fivian (12 August 1931 – 15 December 2021) was a Swiss gymnast. He competed in the 1952 and 1960 Summer Olympics, winning a silver medal in 1952. Fivian died on 15 December 2021, at the age of 90.

Ernst Dokupil (born 24 April 1947) is a retired Austrian footballer and coach. Dokupil started his career with SC Wacker Wien and after merging for FC Admira/Wacker. After one year with 1. Simmeringer SC he went to SK Rapid Wien. In 1976 he went back to Simmering where he played two seasons. In 1978 he became coach of Simmering. In 1981 he won the 2nd league and Simmering was promoted to the Bundesliga. He then went to Admira/Wacker. From 1987 to 1989 he was coach of First Vienna FC. In 1994 he became manager of SK Rapid Wien. In his first season as coach Rapid won the Austrian Cup. The next season Rapid reached the final of the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup. In the 1997–98 he became sports director of Rapid. After Heribert Weber was fired he became again coach of Rapid for the 2000–01 season. 2× Austrian Cup: 1976 (as player), 1995 (as coach) 1× Final of the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup: 1996

Ernst Kaltenbrunner (5 June 1937 – 11 July 1967) was an Austrian football player. He played for Wiener AC, Admira Wien and the Austrian national football team. Ernst Kaltenbrunner started his football career at the Sportvereinigung Zellerndorf where he was a founding member of the first team in 1952. In 1955–56 he went to SK Admira Wien as a center forward where he scored 15 league goals in his debut season. His most successful time was at the WAC where he played since 1957. In the three seasons between 1958 and 1961 he scored 74 goals in the A-League. Together with his younger brother Günter Kaltenbrunner he went back to Admira in 1961. He played just a few matches and went back to WAC in 1963. In 1965 the club was relegated. Kaltenbrunner was not able to play because he had a serious illness. He became youth coach at SV Schwechat and died just a few days after his 30th birthday in 1967. He played only one match for the team on 12 December 1960 in Naples. He scored the winning goal in a 2-1 away win over Italy. Scores and results list Austrias's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Kaltenbrunnergoal.

Ernst-Joachim Küppers (24 August 1942 – 5 February 2025) was a German swimmer. He competed in two events at the 1964 Summer Olympics. He won the silver medal in 1964. He was born in Halle, Gau Halle-Merseburg, Germany. Ernst-Joachim Küppers died on 5 February 2025 in Herne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany at the age of 82.

Ernst Dospel (born 8 October 1976 ) is a former Austrian football player. He played mainly for FK Austria Wien. He also played for the Austrian national football team. He began his career in 1986 at SV Absdorf. The defender moved to FK Austria Wien in 1995. There he played till 2006. During this time he won Austrian championships twice. On August 31, 2006, he signed a six-month contract with SK Sturm Graz. After this time, he moved to FC Superfund.In the summer of 2007 he went to SV Ried. In the summer of 2008, Ernst Dospel finally moved to FC Admira Wacker Mödling in the second-tier Erste Liga. After Admira failed to reach the Bundesliga in the spring of 2010, Ernst Dospel had to leave. From June 2010, he led SV Absdorf as player-coach and was then briefly its sporting director in 2011. On January 26, 2011, he returned to professional football and signed a contract with Austrian second-tier club First Vienna FC. In the summer of 2013 Dospel was released from Vienna due to his ongoing injury problems. Thereafter he moved to the 2nd division club SV Haitzendorf. Ernst Dospel played 19 matches for the Austrian national football team. His first match was on 29 March 2000 versus Sweden. His last match was on 17 August 2005 versus Scotland.

Ernst Kozlicek (27 January 1931 in Vienna- 16 August 2023 in Vienna) was an Austrian football player. He also played in the Austrian national football team. Ernst Kozlicek began his career in 1949 at SC Wacker Wien. His younger brother Paul Kozlicek later joined this team. He was usually listed as "Kozlicek I," to distinguish him from his brother Paul, who was listed as "Kozlicek II." In 1959, the two Kozlicek brothers moved from the financially troubled SC Wacker Wien to Linzer ASK. Their paths separated in 1962. While Paul Kozlicek remained in Linz, Ernst Kozlicek went to 1. Schwechater SC. He ended his career 1966 after one season with SK Sturm Graz. He played 11 matches for Austria. His first match was in a 1-4 loss versus Hungary on 14 November 1954. His last match was in a 2-2 versus England on 14 November 1954. He played two matches at the1958 FIFA World Cup in Sweden.
